title: Offboard session compactification — labnotes
content:
Purpose
Quick labnotes exploring a compact delta/compactification format for offboarded session state. The goal: minimize storage and network while preserving resumability, deterministic replay, and provenance for debugging. This is a personal scratchpad — not final.

Context / constraints
- Sessions can be long; we should avoid storing full turn history for offload.
- Resume must allow: warm (hot prefix), partial KV restore, and deterministic replay for QA.
- Storage targets: S3 objects (gzip), blobstore in Private deployments, and a fast index store (Bigtable/Spanner analog).
- Keep the format backward-compatible for 3 months of rollouts.
- Must include minimal telemetry markers to allow cost attribution when rehydrated.

High-level idea
- Keep a small manifest for each offboarded session: manifest points to 1..N compact blobs. Each compact blob encodes: base_ref (optional), operations (with tombstones), small prefix snapshot, and a compact KV diff map.
- Each blob optimized for sequential streaming and independent rehydration. Blobs are append-only and immutable.
- Allow optional checkpoint markers for fast-path resume (i.e., full snapshot inside the blob).

Sketch: minimal manifest (textual)
{
  "session_id": "s_3a9f...",
  "offboarded_at": "2025-08-14T12:20:00Z",
  "blobs": [
    {"id": "b0000001", "start_token": 1200, "end_token": 1780, "size": 12845, "compression": "gzip"},
    {"id": "b0000002", "start_token": 1781, "end_token": 3200, "size": 22452, "compression": "gzip"}
  ],
  "resume_policy": "prefer_latest_checkpoint",
  "provenance": {"creator":"api-user-123", "request_id":"rq_aaabbb"}
}
Note: manifest above is illustrative; actual JSON stored separately in index store.

Compact blob layout (stream-friendly)
- Header (magic + version + blob_id)
- Optional base_blob_ref (string) — if present client can or cannot pull base.
- Small prefix snapshot (first ~2KB of prefix tokens, tokenized) — used to seed KV cache quickly.
- KV-delta section: list of (key_hash, delta_bytes) where delta_bytes are compressed protobuf deltas. Keys are ordered by hash for binary search.
- Event/op stream: run-length encoded ops: {op_type, seq, payload_len, payload} — supports: USER_MSG, MODEL_TOKEN_APPEND, TOOL_CALL, METADATA_TOGGLE, TTL_UPDATE, CHECKPOINT_MARKER.
- Footer: signature / checksum and small telemetry envelope.

API shape ideas (resume / list / compactify)
1) POST /v1/sessions/:id/compactify
   - body: {"target_size_bytes": 16_384, "checkpoint_frequency": 500, "strategy": "heuristic-preserve-instr"}
   - returns: 202 Accepted + job_id
   - job status: GET /v1/sessions/:id/compactify/:job_id -> {status, blobs_created, estimate_reduction}

2) GET /v1/sessions/:id/manifest
   - returns manifest (as above) or 404 if active session

3) POST /v1/sessions/:id/resume
   - body: {"resume_mode":"fast_prefix_only" | "full_rehydrate" | "replay_from_token", "token": 1782}
   - returns: streaming rehydrate protocol: chunked frames with headers: {frame_type, seq, cursor_token}

Example resume request/response (fast_prefix_only mode)
Request:
POST /v1/sessions/s_3a9f.../resume
{"resume_mode":"fast_prefix_only"}

Response stream frames (2 frames)
FRAME 1: {"frame_type": "prefix_snapshot", "length": 1892} <raw_bytes_gzip>
FRAME 2: {"frame_type": "kv_index_small", "length": 112} <index bytes>

Client notes: if prefix contains tokenizer IDs we can skip fetch to model store — seed the runtime KV quickly and respond with 200 + ephemeral session token. Fall back to full_rehydrate if access pattern needs older context.

Compact delta example (text pseudo-json for readability)
[
  {"seq": 1201, "op": "MODEL_TOKEN_APPEND", "tokens": [101, 101, 4789]},
  {"seq": 1205, "op": "METADATA_TOGGLE", "key": "safety_labels", "value": null},
  {"seq": 1210, "op": "KV_PUT", "key_hash": "h_7c3a", "value_delta_len": 48}
]

Design tradeoffs / questions
- Key hashing: use siphash64 vs murmur? Need stable across languages. Prefer siphash with explicit seed and store seed in manifest.
- Should we allow blobs to reference other blobs (base refs)? Pro: dedupe common base snapshots. Con: increases read fan-out at resume. Probably allow but prefer single-level chains max depth 2.
- Encryption: blobs may be KMS-encrypted; but index must store unencrypted minimal metadata for query. For Private deployments, we need on-prem KMS integration.
- Garbage collection: keep last N compact blobs or by TTL. Need a GC policy to avoid stale chained references.

Operational thoughts
- Telemetry: embed a tiny envelope: {compact_ops_count, unique_keys, estimated_tokens_saved, cpu_ms} for quick billing/chargeback. Keep it COMPACT.
- Monitoring: track time_to_first_byte on resume, full_rehydrate_rate, and number of blobs read per resume.
- Rollout plan sketch: start as opt-in flag on Dedicated clusters; expose a few export/import hooks for internal tools.

ASCII diagram (runtime interaction)
Client -> Ingress -> Router
                |           |
                v           v
            Session API    Orchestrator
                |           |
                v           v
            Compactify job -> Blobstore (S3 or on-prem)
                             Index store
                ^
                | resume request
                v
            Serving runtime (seeded with prefix + kv deltas)

Open questions / TODOs (short action list)
- [ ] Pick canonical key-hash function and record seed (E2).
- [ ] Small PoC: implement writer that emits header + kv delta + ops stream (Diego taking) — target: proof of <3s resume for 5k-token sessions.
- [ ] Add deterministic serializer for op payloads so replay tests can pass.
- [ ] Wire minimal telemetry to billing path (product ask) — talk to Priya.
- [ ] Add unit tests for chained-base blobs (depth 2) and GC interactions.

Notes to self
- Keep format stable enough for 2 quarters; we can add opt-in features via header flags.
- When in doubt, prefer single-file per-checkpoint blobs (even if slightly larger) for resume simplicity.

References
- Related RFC: INF-453 (see linked artifacts)
- Initial writer prototype: github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/tree/compact-write-experiment

Unresolved trade-offs (capture)
- Should checksum be computed on compressed bytes or raw bytes? Compressed gives faster verification on reader but means different runtime implementations must match compression. Leaning towards compressed-checksum + store a small uncompressed length.

End of notes.

(If this becomes useful, move to a formal spec: fields, wire-types, test vectors.)
